newsitem.title: UK: Frankfurt closes at record, London recovers.
newsitem.headline: Frankfurt closes at record, London recovers.

text.p: German stocks soared to a closing record on Thursday as the stronger dollar boosted export prospects and most other European bourses recovered from the previous day's losses.
On currency markets, the dollar remained mostly buoyant around the 1.56 mark level after a decision by the Bundesbank to keeps rates on hold. It later slipped slightly.
Frankfurt was in sparkling form throughout the day and closed at a high of 2909.91 points, eclipsing the previous best of 2866.07 set only two days ago.
"The rally is feeding the rally," said one trader.

"The fact that the dollar has stabilised at its new highs has been encouraging," said another, referring to the dollar's rally to 23-month highs this week above 1.57 marks and then settling around 1.56 marks, boosting shares in German exporting stocks.

The link between Frankfurt's bourse and the strength of the dollar was shown in post-bourse dealings when the computerised IBIS DAX slipped from record highs to trade under 2,900 points as the dollar lost ground.
German government figures showing a higher-than-expected climb in unemployment eased inflation worries and helped spread the market's optimistic mood.
And year-end buying by German institutional investors -- some had been left behind in the speed of the current climb -- added to the buying frenzy, dealers said.
"The rally is not over yet. We're still in a bullish phase and there's still potential in many stocks. The DAX could make 3,000 points by the year end," said a trader.
The buying spree has been fuelled in the last two weeks by the firmer dollar and German government bond strength, sparked by fresh speculation that German interest rates may still have room to fall.
But the DAX held onto most of its gains despite the Bundesbank announcement that it had held key interest rates.
In London, stocks rebounded amid fresh falls in sterling and as comments from Bank of England governor Eddie George eased worries about an imminent sharp rise in British interest rates.
The pound's second sharp decline of the week eased worries that the currency's strength would further squeeze the overseas earnings of leading international stocks.

George told a committee of legislators he did not believe Britain was on the verge of a 1980s-style boom. Though a rate rise was needed before the election due by next May, "we don't see an urgent need for a dramatic step," he said.
Paris was the only leading bourse to show a decline. It fell 0.6 percent on disappointment at the Bundesbank's decision to hold rates. Some traders had been counting on a small increase.
On currency markets, the dollar slipped slightly to 1.5562 marks in midafternoon but had been buoyant for most of the session. The pound fell against the mark and dollar.

The U.S. currency remained weak against the yen after it suffered in overnight trade because of remarks from former vice finance minister Makoto Utsumi that the Bank of Japan was seeking an increase in interest rates as soon as possible.

Sterling fell against the dollar and over four pfennigs against the mark in early trade before recovering slighty. It was at $1.6277 in midafternoon after touching $1.6103. It stood at $1.6415 late on Wednesday.
Dealers attributed the pound's fresh falls to more profit-taking from its recent highs combined with George's remarks about British interest rates.
CURRENCIES AT 1530 GMT
The dollar was quoted at 112.63 yen and 1.5562 marks against 113.28 yen and 1.5638 marks in late Europe on Wednesday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1530 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE 100 index of leading British shares was up 15.7 points at 4,060.9.
PARIS - The CAC-40 share index was down 17.07 points at 2,291.58.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index closed up 43.84 points at 2,909.91.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold fixed in the afternoon at $369.00, compared to $369.95 at Wednesday's close. Silver was at $4.80, down two cents.
